nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. For every $y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the adjoint $C^*$ of $C$ satisfies
nodes.title: Adjoint of the Cesàro operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ be the first standard basis vector. Then $C^* e_0 = e_0$, where $C^*$ is the adjoint of $C$.
nodes.title: The adjoint of the Cesàro operator fixes the first basis vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $(Cx)_n = \bigl(\sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k\bigr)/(n + 1)$.
nodes.title: Formula for the Cesàro operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ be the first standard basis vector. With coordinates indexed from $0$, $(C e_0)_1 = 1/2$.
nodes.title: Second coordinate of the Cesàro operator at the first basis vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the Cesàro operator, as a continuous linear map on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, takes the same value at $x$ as the Cesàro linear map, the same averaging map considered only as a linear map.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator agrees with the Cesàro linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is injective.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator is injective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $e_n$ be the standard basis vector with $1$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ elsewhere. For all $n, k \in \mathbb{N}$, $(C e_n)_k = 1/(k + 1)$ if $n \le k$, and $(C e_n)_k = 0$ if $k < n$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator on standard basis vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $t_N$ be the test vector whose first $N$ coordinates equal $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. For all $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $N \le n$, $(C t_N)_n = N (\sqrt{N})^{-1}/(n + 1)$, where $(\sqrt{0})^{-1}$ is read as $0$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator on a test vector, past its support

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $t_N$ be the test vector whose first $N$ coordinates equal $1/\sqrt{N}$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. For all $n, N \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n < N$, $(C t_N)_n = 1/\sqrt{N}$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator on a test vector, within its support

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ is the continuous linear map from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself that sends a sequence $x$ to its sequence of averages, $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. It is obtained from the Cesàro linear map with the bound $\|Cx\| \le 2 \|x\|$.
nodes.title: Cesàro operator on square-summable sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $n$, the element $n + 1$ of $\mathbb{K}$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: The Cesàro denominator $n + 1$ is nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $e_0 \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ be the first standard basis vector. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $e_0(n) = 1$ if $n = 0$ and $e_0(n) = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the first standard basis vector of $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The vector $e_0 \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the sequence with $e_0(0) = 1$ and $e_0(n) = 0$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The first standard basis vector of $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $C$ from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself that sends a sequence $x$ to its sequence of Cesàro means, $(Cx)(n) = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th Cesàro mean of $x$ is the average of its first $n + 1$ terms, $\frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k)$.
nodes.title: Cesàro means of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $y$ be the alternating harmonic sequence, viewed as an element of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $y(n) = (-1)^n / (n + 1)$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the alternating harmonic sequence in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The sequence $y$ with $y(n) = (-1)^n / (n + 1)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is square-summable, and it is regarded as an element of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The alternating harmonic sequence in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $x(n+1) = (n+2)\,(Cx)(n+1) - (n+1)\,(Cx)(n)$.
nodes.title: One step of inverting the Cesàro operator

nodes.summary: For $\mathbb{K}$ equal to $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, this is the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, with the norm $\|x\| = \left(\sum_{n} |x(n)|^2\right)^{1/2}$.
nodes.title: The sequence space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k) = (n+1)\,(Cx)(n)$.
nodes.title: Partial sums from Cesàro means

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $N$ and $j$ be natural numbers. The $j$-th coordinate of the Cesàro test vector $t_N \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is $1/\sqrt{N}$ if $j < N$, and $0$ if $j \ge N$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the Cesàro test vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For a natural number $N$, the test vector $t_N = \sum_{i < N} \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} e_i$ has coordinate $1/\sqrt{N}$ at each $j < N$ and $0$ at each $j \ge N$; in particular $t_0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Cesàro test vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $t_N$ be the $N$-th Cesàro test vector. For every natural number $N \ge 1$, $\|C t_N\|^2 \ge 5/4$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the Cesàro operator on the test vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, then the sequence of its Cesàro means $n \mapsto \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$ also lies in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Cesàro means preserve square-summability

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$, has operator norm $\|C\| \le 2$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator has norm at most 2

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $n$, the element $n + 1$ of $\mathbb{K}$ (the denominator of the $n$-th Cesàro mean) has norm equal to the real number $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Norm of the Cesàro denominator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The first standard basis vector $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has norm $\|e_0\| = 1$.
nodes.title: The first basis vector is a unit vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, viewed as a linear map, given by $(Cx)_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, $\|Cx\| \le 2 \|x\|$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator is bounded by 2

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be any sequence and let $n$ be a natural number. Then $\|\frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k\| \le \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \|x_k\|$.
nodes.title: A Cesàro mean is bounded by the mean of the norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $N$, the norm of $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$, computed in $\mathbb{K}$, equals the real number $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$; for $N = 0$ both sides are $0$, with the convention $0^{-1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Norm of the Cesàro test-vector coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $N \ge 1$, the test vector $t_N \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, equal to $1/\sqrt{N}$ at the coordinates $0, \dots, N - 1$ and to $0$ elsewhere, has norm $\|t_N\| = 1$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro test vectors are unit vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is not a compact operator.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator is not compact

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is not self-adjoint.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator is not self-adjoint

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The sequence $y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with $y_n = (-1)^n/(n + 1)$ is not in the range of the Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. In particular $C$ is not surjective.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator is not surjective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, has operator norm $\|C\| \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro operator has norm at least one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the Cesàro means $\sigma_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$ satisfy: the series $\sum_n |\sigma_n|^2$ converges.
nodes.title: Cesàro means of square-summable sequences are square-summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, and for $N \ge 1$ let $t_N$ be the vector equal to $1/\sqrt{N}$ at the coordinates $0, \dots, N - 1$ and to $0$ elsewhere. Then for every fixed coordinate $n$, $(C t_{N+1})_n \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The Cesàro images of the test vectors tend to zero coordinatewise
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
